issues.title: FR3 (focused+selected keeps the select accent) has no test that bites - TestSelectedAndFocusedBothVisible passes with the wiring deleted
issues.description:
cli/internal/tui/card_selection_test.go:135-159. The test's own comment claims it pins that "the focused+selected frame style stays on the select accent", and the plan's Tests table names it as FR3's guard. Its render-level assertions are only `strings.Contains(out, "\u2713")` and `strings.Contains(out, "\u2551")`; the select-accent claim is asserted against `columnStyles[i].cardFocusedSelected.GetBorderTopForeground()`, i.e. against the STYLE VALUE, never against what renderCard picks. Both render assertions still hold if renderCard falls back to `cardFocused` (the column accent): the ✓ comes from `selMarkStyle.Render("✓ ")` in the body regardless of the frame, and ║ comes from any double-border style. Mutation verified: deleting `case focused && selected: style = columnStyles[colIdx].cardFocusedSelected` from cli/internal/tui/view.go:770-771 leaves the ENTIRE cli/internal/tui suite green (only the unrelated, path-dependent TestTemplateScaffoldRendersNoCorrelationChip fails in the out-of-tree copy). This is exactly code-review-standards.md #11(b) - "a wiring was named in the plan, shipped, and had no test that bites" - and #11's "a test whose comment claims coverage its assertions do not provide". The production code is correct today; nothing stops it from silently regressing.

[Round 2 verification] VERIFIED. Re-ran the exact mutation (deleted the `case focused && selected:` arm from renderCard in view.go): `go test ./ -run TestSelectedAndFocusedBothVisible` now FAILS at card_selection_test.go:168 - "focused+selected card renders the focused-only frame — the select accent was swallowed: \x1b[38;5;111m╔…" (the blue column-0 accent). Restored; suite green (`go test ./internal/tui/` ok, 7.8s) and `git diff` byte-identical to pre-check. The column-0 choice is sound: columnAccent[2] Dark #5db97a == selectAccent Dark #5db97a (styles.go:46-57), so column 2 could not separate the two arms, while column 0 (#2f6fe0/#7aa8ff blue) differs from the select green under BOTH light and dark adaptive resolutions.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Make the assertion name the exact reason. Cheapest honest form: inside TestSelectedAndFocusedBothVisible call `forceColors(t)` and compare renders - assert that the focused+selected card's border SGR run equals the one produced by `lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(selectAccent).Render("║")` and that the focused-only card of the SAME column renders a DIFFERENT border colour (so the two arms cannot collapse). Alternative, per code-review-standards #11(a): extract the frame decision into a package-level pure func `cardFrame(colIdx int, focused, selected bool) lipgloss.Style` used by renderCard, and assert `cardFrame(2,true,true)` == `columnStyles[2].cardFocusedSelected` and `cardFrame(2,true,false)` == `columnStyles[2].cardFocused`. Re-run the mutation (delete the focused&&selected branch) and prove at least one test fails.
issues.fix_summary: TestSelectedAndFocusedBothVisible now forces colours and compares rendered TOP BORDERS on column 0 (blue - ready col 2 shares selectAccent by palette design): deleting the focused&&selected arm makes both renders equal and the test fail.

issues.title: FR5's plans-tab focus cue is unguarded - renderPlanCard can stop marking focus entirely with the suite green
issues.description:
cli/internal/tui/plans_tab.go:1375-1379 is the only thing that makes a focused plan card distinguishable (`if focused { style = columnStyles[colIdx].cardFocused }`). The plan's mirror test TestFocusedPlanCardKeepsInnerColors (card_selection_test.go:204-222) compares the focused vs unfocused INNER body only - and since the change made the body focus-independent by construction, that comparison can only ever catch a fill regression on the frame, never the loss of the cue itself. Mutation verified: replacing that block with `style := columnStyles[colIdx].card; _ = focused` leaves the whole cli/internal/tui suite green. renderPlanCard has no other test reference in the package (grep: only card_selection_test.go:209-210). The work board has TestFocusedCardMarkedByBorderGlyph for exactly this; the plans board, which FR5 says gets "the identical treatment", has no equivalent - and the cue is the NFR Diagnosability bar (it must be a glyph, assertable in View()).

[Round 2 verification] VERIFIED. Re-ran the exact mutation (`style := columnStyles[colIdx].card` + `_ = focused` in renderPlanCard): `go test ./ -run TestFocusedPlanCardKeepsInnerColors` now FAILS at card_selection_test.go:242 - "focused plan card missing the double focus border" (the render shows the rounded ╭─╮ set). The mirrored negative assertion (an unfocused card must NOT carry ║) is present too, so the inverse regression (always-focused frame) is covered as well. Restored; tree byte-identical.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Add a small guard next to TestFocusedPlanCardKeepsInnerColors, e.g. TestFocusedPlanCardMarkedByBorderGlyph: with the default (colourless) go-test render, `m.renderPlanCard(2, p, true, 40)` must contain "║", "═" and "╔", and `m.renderPlanCard(2, p, false, 40)` must contain "│" and neither "║" nor "═" - the exact shape TestFocusedCardMarkedByBorderGlyph already uses for the work board. Confirm it bites by re-running the `_ = focused` mutation.
issues.fix_summary: TestFocusedPlanCardKeepsInnerColors now also asserts the focused plan card render contains the double-border glyphs and the unfocused one does not - a renderPlanCard ignoring `focused` fails.

issues.title: FR6's config-tab rows are unguarded - re-adding a focus fill to the project/source rows keeps the suite green
issues.description:
cli/internal/tui/config_tab.go:320-346 (project rows) and :353-376 (source rows) are the D2 half of this change: the focus fill was dropped so the origin dots keep their tint, and focus is now carried by the `▸ ` cursor + a slugStyle name. Nothing pins that. Mutation verified: restoring `dot := "●"` for the focused source row and wrapping the row in `Foreground(focusFg).Background(focusBg).Bold(true)` leaves the whole cli/internal/tui suite green. The only test that touches viewConfigLeft is TestConfigSwitcherRowTruncatedToPane (config_screen_test.go:437-459), which asserts row WIDTH only. The changelog half of FR6 does have a guard (TestFocusedChangelogRowKeepsColors) - the config half does not, so half of the accepted D2 fork ships uncovered.

[Round 2 verification] VERIFIED for the finding's named mutation. The new TestFocusedConfigRowsKeepColors (card_selection_test.go:254-278) bites: re-adding `dot := "●"` + the `Foreground(focusFg).Background(focusBg).Bold(true)` row fill on the focused source row FAILS at :272 ("focused config row lost its styled origin dot"), printing the de-tinted row `\x1b[1;38;5;231;48;5;17m▸ ● svc …`. Restored; tree byte-identical.

[Residual, recorded not re-opened - nit] The guard is one notch weaker than the title's broadest reading: a fill-ONLY regression (the row wrapped in Foreground(focusFg).Background(focusBg) while projectOriginDots/sourceDot keep their own tint) still PASSES on both the project and the source row - checked by mutation this round. The rendered row in that case is `\x1b[1;38;5;231;48;5;17m▸ \x1b[38;5;179m●\x1b[0m …`, i.e. exactly the torn background the colStyleSet comment in styles.go warns about (the fill dies at the first inner reset). Closing it is the one line the round-1 proposal marked optional: assert no `▸` row carries a background SGR (`\x1b\[[0-9;]*48;`). Left as a note for a future round rather than a new issue, per this round's delta scope.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Add one test in the FR6 shape of TestFocusedChangelogRowKeepsColors: with forceColors(t) and a project whose focused source has a registry colour, render viewConfigLeft() and assert (a) the focused source row still contains the ANSI-styled `●` fragment that m.sourceDot(name) produces (i.e. the tint survives focus), and (b) the focused row carries the `▸ ` cursor. Optionally assert no row contains the focusBg background sequence. Prove it bites with the fill mutation above.
issues.fix_summary: New TestFocusedConfigRowsKeepColors: seeded config tab, forced colours; every focused (▸) row must carry an individually-SGR-styled ● - a restored row fill (one sequence for the whole row) fails the regexp.

issues.title: Two comments still describe constructs this change deleted (gateBorder, the changelog "selection bar")
issues.description:
cli/internal/tui/model.go:1469 - stripeAccent's doc comment says "The renderer recolors the heavy-`┃` gateBorder with it." `gateBorder` was deleted from styles.go by this change; the renderer now composes the stripe over the focus/selection border via GetBorderStyle() (view.go:779-783). A comment naming a symbol that no longer exists is the exact drift code-review-standards.md #1 says to grep for. cli/internal/tui/view.go:333-335 - renderChangelogColumn's comment still says the focused row "gets the ▸ cursor + selection bar"; the selection bar (changelogFocusStyle) is gone and the row is now cursor + bright slug only, which is what changelogRow's own updated comment (view.go:365-368) correctly states. Both were missed by the otherwise thorough comment sweep in this diff.

[Round 2 verification] VERIFIED. model.go:1467-1470 now reads "The renderer overrides the chosen border set's Left edge with the heavy `┃` and recolors it with this" (no `gateBorder`); view.go:333-335 now reads "gets the ▸ cursor + a bright slug". `grep -rn gateBorder cli/` returns nothing at all. `grep -rn "selection bar" cli/` has exactly one survivor and it is a TEST comment - cli/internal/tui/redesign_test.go:191, TestChangelogFocusCursor's header "(▸ cursor + selection bar)" - so the non-test bar set for this round is met. That line is the same class of stale drift (its test body only asserts the ▸ cursor, so the comment over-claims); nit-level, outside this finding's named scope, recorded here rather than raised as a new issue.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. model.go:1469 -> "The renderer overrides just the chosen border's Left edge with the heavy `┃` gateStripe and recolors it with this accent (view.go), so the stripe composes over the focus/selection frame." view.go:334 -> drop "+ selection bar", e.g. "gets the ▸ cursor (and a bright slug), so navigating the list has an in-list indicator, not just the footer text." Then re-grep `gateBorder` and `selection bar` across cli/ to confirm nothing else survives.
issues.fix_summary: model.go stripeAccent comment now describes the Left-edge override composition; view.go renderChangelogColumn comment now says "▸ cursor + a bright slug". Re-grepped gateBorder + "selection bar" across cli/ - no survivors.
